A Survey of Modern NLP Techniques

1. Introduction

Natural language processing has advanced significantly in recent years. The Transformer architecture [1] revolutionized the field by replacing recurrence with self-attention. Building on this, pre-trained language models like BERT [2] achieved state-of-the-art results across many benchmarks.

Several works have explored the application of these models to downstream tasks [1, 3]. The combination of pre-training and fine-tuning has become the standard paradigm in NLP.

2. Methods

Our approach follows the standard fine-tuning methodology described in [2]. We evaluate on the standard benchmarks used by Smith et al. (2020).

3. Conclusion

The field continues to advance with new architectures and larger models.

References

[1] Vaswani, A., Shazeer, N., Parmar, N., Uszkoreit, J., Jones, L., Gomez, A. N., Kaiser, L., and Polosukhin, I. (2017). Attention is All You Need. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 30.

[2] Devlin, J., Chang, M., Lee, K., and Toutanova, K. (2019). BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding. Proceedings of NAACL-HLT.

[3] Brown, T. B., Mann, B., Ryder, N., and Subbiah, M. (2020). Language Models are Few-Shot Learners. arXiv:2005.14165.
